facts.t: Red drum (redfish): live shrimp.
Spotted seatrout: live shrimp, or small pinfish or pigfish (grunts), free-lined near the bottom to draw trout out of grass-bed holes.
Sheepshead: live shrimp, sand fleas or fiddler crabs.
Black drum: cut bait, shrimp, sand fleas or blue crabs.
Snook: live pinfish, small mullet, shrimp or sardines.
Channel catfish: strong-smelling baits such as chicken liver or gizzards, shrimp, cut mullet and commercial stinkbaits.
From a pier: use a weighted rig with natural bait such as shrimp to catch a variety of species off the bottom.

Jigging is one of the oldest and most popular fishing techniques and gives the appearance of an injured fish.
To jig, cast out and let your jig sink to the bottom. Snap or flick your rod sideways or up and down, then let the jig sink back to the bottom.
Jigging is a popular inshore and offshore method that can lead to success with many different species.
